newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil slump on crude, futures.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil slump on crude, futures.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were down sharply midday Monday on big falls to crude and product futures in the West, brokers said.
"The market collapsed because of the heating oil collapse on NYMEX," one broker said.
Gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.00/$25.20 per barrel down sharply from Friday's $25.75/$25.85. The market traded earlier today at $25.00, brokers said
March was last quoted at $25.60/$25.80 per barrel from Friday's $26.40/$26.60 and traded earlier at $26.00 and $25.85.

The market's collapse was triggered by falling futures prices where February Brent crude lost 66 cents to close at $22.52 per barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange while February gas oil was down $2.75 per tonne to $209.25 on Friday.

The falls were carried into trading in New York where heating oil closed down 1.69 cents per gallon on NYMEX on Friday and continued to trek downward on the afterhours ACCESS where it lost another 51 cents to last trade at 65.65.
Traders said fundamentals remain weak with several sellers seen still holding on to prompt cargoes in the absence of new regional demand.
In the physical market on Friday one 150,000-barrel cargo traded at $25.30 per barrel free-on-board Singapore--a 40 cent discount to prevailing swap prices.
Fuel oil swaps were quoted down slightly at $98.50/$99.75 per tonne, down about $1.00 from Friday.
Naphtha was down sharply in line with the big falls to crude prices with February buyers seen at $24.20 per barrel from Friday's $24.85/$25.10 per barrel, one broker said.
